purpose: Synthetic-data baseline only. These standardized priors are not clinical effect estimates or dietary recommendations.

outcomes.description: Standardized synthetic sleep-disruption score; higher means more disruption.
Standardized synthetic post-meal glucose-response score; higher means a larger response.
Standardized synthetic blood-pressure response score; higher means a larger response.

evidence.citation: Gardiner et al., The effect of caffeine on subsequent sleep: A systematic review and meta-analysis, 2023.
evidence.interpretation: Caffeine was associated with shorter and less efficient subsequent sleep; timing and dose matter.

priors.simulation_note: The mean is a standardized simulation parameter, not the study's clinical effect size.

evidence.citation: Zeevi et al., Personalized Nutrition by Prediction of Glycemic Responses, 2015.
evidence.interpretation: Post-meal glucose responses vary substantially between people; nutrient content alone is insufficient for individual prediction.

priors.simulation_note: This prior is only valid for a CGM-derived response outcome, not for sleep or heart-rate data.

evidence.interpretation: Lower dietary sodium within the trial context was associated with lower ambulatory blood pressure.

priors.simulation_note: A consumer watch does not generally measure blood pressure reliably enough for this outcome; use a validated BP measurement source.
